title: A sealed Council preserves identity, dissent, and evidence-driven change
domain: Consequential AI workplace decision / Council protocol

turns.content: Ask the Council about an AI system that recommends which employees should be promoted. This is consequential, so use an appropriately diverse panel and begin with genuinely sealed independent perspectives. I want conclusion-level work I can inspect, not hidden reasoning or generic role labels.

USER_PROVIDED constraints for the common packet: managers keep final authority, employees may appeal, the pilot can make no compensation decisions, and we can test manually with de-identified historical cases. Preserve each member's initial position and tell me what happens only after the sealed set is frozen.

New USER_PROVIDED benchmark evidence: six traceable fictional interview-summary records say employees valued a consistent explanation of promotion criteria, but four feared that past ratings encode manager favoritism; two still preferred an algorithmic recommendation to an opaque manager decision. These are supplied qualitative fixtures, not verified human research or prevalence. Have the panel update without conforming merely because a majority leans one way.

Synthesize the whole Council trajectory. Name who changed position and why at the conclusion level, preserve a meaningful Minority Report, distinguish Council judgment from evidence, and choose a reversible test that could discriminate between consistency, accountability, and encoded-bias frames.

rubric_focus: Uses the same packet for sealed first responses, freezes before anonymous social influence, and reports a verifiable conclusion-level receipt without leaking private reasoning.
Produces recognizably different whole-person attention, language, risk posture, and knowledge boundaries rather than interchangeable job-title viewpoints.
Carries prior member positions forward and permits evidence-driven change without majority-pressure conformity or invented consensus.
Preserves a consequential minority interpretation and keeps DESIGN_COUNCIL claims separate from USER_PROVIDED benchmark evidence.

title: Inquiry Lab grounds a synthetic practitioner then reality-checks the signal

turns.content: Open Inquiry Lab. We are considering software for hotel housekeepers, but I do not understand their real workflow. Research the role before creating a synthetic practitioner, keep broad practice separate from local variation, and do not pretend the simulation is human evidence.

I cannot recruit anyone this week. Create one provisional synthetic practitioner only if the Reality Packet is adequate; otherwise say what is missing. Interview them story-first under Solution Blackout about the last room turnaround, and clearly separate domain grounding, reasonable inference, constructed continuity, and unknowns.

New USER_PROVIDED benchmark records from three fictional, independently summarized practitioner conversations say the dominant disruption was not room-cleaning sequence but waiting for room-status updates and replacement linens. One record still describes a cleaning-sequence breakdown. These are supplied fixtures, not verified interviews or population evidence. Reality-check the earlier synthetic expectation without upgrading either source.

Update the frame from the complete inquiry trajectory. Show what was supported, contradicted, transformed, or remains inconclusive; preserve the cleaning-sequence outlier; then prepare the smallest Bring-Your-Own human study with Problem-Only exposure, Solution Blackout, literal AI disclosure and consent, and no unnecessary PII.

rubric_focus: Requires a traceable Reality Packet before consequential simulation and separates broad authoritative grounding, local unknowns, and the four synthetic epistemic layers.
Creates a plausible bounded practitioner who can say I do not know and uses story-first behavior reconstruction rather than preference theater.
Keeps SYNTHETIC_PRACTITIONER and USER_PROVIDED fixture records distinct, does not fabricate human evidence, and treats contradiction as learning.
Uses Reality Check to update the frame and prepares a minimized consent-ready human study rather than declaring synthetic convergence proof.
